text.p: These are the stories making headlines in the Namibian newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

* Seven people have been killed by the Namibian security forces in the north-west of the country since 1994, a government investigation revealed. The investigation was launched in response to a report by the National Society for Human Rights, (NSHR), which claimed 1,768 people, mostly Angolans, had been killed or disappeared.
* Sixteen torture charges, brought by prisoners against members of the police in the far north, have been finalised.

* A group of !Kung San in the Caprivi are fighting for survival. The group, which a couple of weeks ago still comprised 260 people, has shrunk to a mere sixty, following an exodus to Angola by the others.

* A gambling war is expected in Namibia with two separate high court cases involving all four casino licence holders. This was confirmed following the conclusion of a government investigation into casinos and gambling.

* An official investigation into claims by the National Society for Human Rights that over 1,700 people disappeared or were killed at the hands of security forces in the Kavango and Caprivi, has found no evidence of such claims.
